title: Anthropic Fast-Tracks AI Bug Reports to OSS Maintainers, Taps 11 Firms for OT Security
key_facts: Anthropic announced two cybersecurity initiatives on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.

OSS Scanner is a free, opt-in service using Anthropic's most capable models to scan open-source projects periodically and send maintainers reports with a proof of concept and, where available, a suggested fix.
Reports are model-generated and sent without human review, so some will contain errors such as wrong severity ratings; Anthropic expects a true-positive rate above 90%.
The Critical Infrastructure Defense Program gives operational-technology providers Claude models, on-site engineers and threat research.
Eleven founding partners include Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, Palo Alto Networks, PwC and Rockwell Automation.
Anthropic says flaws found through Project Glasswing often took months to fix and that it has not yet cut cyber risk enough.
Operational technology often cannot be taken offline to patch, so known flaws can stay unfixed for years.
quote_evidence: Maintainers have to opt in to have their projects scanned.
It expects a true-positive rate above 90% and aims to improve it over time.
Anthropic noted that OT systems often cannot be taken offline for patching, so known vulnerabilities can remain unresolved for years.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster AI-found bug reports for open-source maintainers and AI help for industrial-security providers, with accuracy claims coming from Anthropic.
notes: Company announcement relayed by one outlet; accuracy figures are Anthropic's own.
